newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WEST INDIES COLLAPSE AGAINST AUSTRALIA XI.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES COLLAPSE AGAINST AUSTRALIA XI.

text.p: West Indies suffered a
demoralising batting collapse on Saturday ahead of next week's
first test and were in danger of being made to bat again in the
four-day match against an Australia XI at Bellerive Oval.
West Indies were 82 for four at the close on the second day
after Australia XI captain Stuart Law declared his side's first
innings closed at 544 for four at tea.
The touring side's collapse followed a savaging at the hands
of
Australia XI openers and aspiring test batsmen Matthew Hayden
and Matthew Elliott, Hayden scoring a double century and Elliott
his second century in a week.
West Indies' innings started badly when opener
Robert Samuels fell to a dazzling catch at point by Hayden from
the bowling of Andrew Bichel for three.
Hayden took another sharp catch to dismiss world record
batsman Brian Lara for a paltry six, again off Bichel.
Pace bowler Anthony Stuart took the wicket of opener
Sherwin Campbell for 18 with his first ball. The West Indies
score stood at 31. Eleven runs later the tourists lost their
fourth wicket when Stuart trapped Shivnarine Chanderpaul leg
before wicket for 15.
Hayden and Elliott, both pushing for inclusion in the first
test in Brisbane beginning next Friday, put their side in a
seemingly unbeatable position with a partnersip of 323, a
first-class record for matches in Hobart.
Hayden eventually fell to part-time bowler Chanderpaul,
caught behind by Courtney Browne for 224.
Elliott added five runs to his overnight score before he was
bowled by an inswinging yorker from Ian Bishop for 158.
Law was the only failure for the Australia XI, trapped leg
before wicket by Jimmy Adams for a duck. Greg Blewett, another
test hopeful, was 89 not out when Law declared.
Elliott scored 187 in a Sheffield Shield match for Victoria
last week and topped Australia's domestic averages last season.
